Sun, Aug 30, 2026
rows.link: If you want to move your content from AI-assisted to AI-run, start here: - Automate the mechanical stuff first. Triggers, connections, the ""check these four tools before proposing anything"" jobs. - Leave your writing alone until it stops needing your corrections. - Do it in that

rows.first: Mon, Oct 5, 2026
Sat, Sep 5, 2026
rows.link: Any serious personal brand who wants $$$ needs to run this analysis: - what worked last week - what didnt Then, map out potential new weekly tests by categorizing: - topic - format - tof/mof/bof

rows.first: Sun, Oct 4, 2026
rows.link: Same gated offer, run three times across two months. 263 comments, then 81, then 34. Reach dropped every time and nobody complained, because tuesday's audience is a different slice than the one from three weeks ago.

rows.first: Tue, Sep 8, 2026
rows.link: Someone asked if they should learn n8n or claude code first. Honestly whichever one you'd actually open on a tuesday when you're behind on client work. I picked claude code because every file I have is already in there, and I was never going to open a canvas UI at 7pm.

rows.first: Mon, Sep 14, 2026
rows.link: The four lowest-reach articles on the account booked 78% of the calls. I only found that because I went back and logged the ones that flopped. For months my capture file was 40 winners out of 41, which tells you what good looks like and nothing about a near miss. One article https://t.co/yNDpfvOGsu

rows.first: Wed, Sep 9, 2026
rows.link: An analysis that names its own blind spot lets you go get the missing data. One that hides the blind spot gets you doubling down, with total confidence, on reach that was never going to convert. https://t.co/1mMtrP7w93

rows.first: Sun, Aug 30, 2026
rows.link: A post with a link in it gets less distribution than a post without one. So the post earns its reach clean, and the ask hangs underneath once it's already moving. Anyone reading that far down already put their hand up.

rows.first: Thu, Sep 3, 2026
Thu, Sep 3, 2026
rows.link: Six things every high-view X article did, after I read the top 50 side by side: illustration covers, concrete titles, long word counts, covers that argue or make you feel, credentials placed late, and the whole method given away for free. Full breakdown below. https://t.co/bNJ5gNspOC

rows.first: Mon, Sep 14, 2026
rows.link: One repo runs our whole inbound. Eleven top-level areas, each with an owner and an entry point, all indexed in one map file. If it's not in the map, the next agent rebuilds it.

rows.first: Thu, Sep 17, 2026
rows.link: Lead magnet test I run before anything ships. If someone reads the whole thing and does nothing differently tomorrow, it failed. Doesn't matter how good the writing was. Almost everything being given away right now fails that.

rows.first: Sun, Sep 20, 2026
rows.link: You said it better on a client call than you'll ever write it at a keyboard. You weren't performing, you were just explaining it to someone who needed to get it. That's the article.
